name: LAVA
aliases: Laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy versus vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy
question: Is laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy noninferior to vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy for symptomatic apical failure or retreatment after surgery for uterine prolapse?

design.population: 126 women with stage 2 or higher uterine prolapse and no prior pelvic floor surgery at six hospitals in the Netherlands and Belgium.
design.locator: Thesis chapter 6, Methods, Study design; Figure 1; PubMed abstract, Population

verdictNote: The upper 95% confidence bound of 3.7 points was below the 10-point noninferiority margin.
takeaway: Laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy was noninferior to vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy for symptomatic apical failure or retreatment at 12 months in women with stage 2 or higher uterine prolapse (1.6% versus 3.3%; risk difference −1.7 percentage points, 95% CI −7.1 to 3.7).

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: van IJsselmuiden MN, van Oudheusden AMJ, Veen J, et al. Hysteropexy in the treatment of uterine prolapse stage 2 or higher: laparoscopic sacrohysteropexy versus sacrospinous hysteropexy—a multicentre randomised controlled trial (LAVA trial). *BJOG.* 2020;127(10):1284-1293. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.16242
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Main outcome measures and Results

results.measure: 12-month symptomatic POP-Q stage 2 or higher apical recurrence and/or repeat surgery or pessary for apical prolapse; intention to treat with last observation carried forward; risk difference in percentage points (laparoscopic minus vaginal)
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin: 10 percentage points. One of 62 randomized women in the vaginal arm had no follow-up data and was excluded from this analysis.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 6, journal pp. 94–99, Methods, Statistical analysis; Figure 1; Table 2

results.measure: 12-month POP-Q stage 2 or higher prolapse in any compartment, pessary use, or repeat surgery; intention to treat with last observation carried forward; risk difference in percentage points (laparoscopic minus vaginal)
results.note: Distinct from the symptomatic apical primary endpoint.

results.measure: 12-month no prolapse beyond hymen in any compartment, no bothersome bulge, and no repeat surgery or pessary; intention to treat with last observation carried forward; risk difference in percentage points (laparoscopic minus vaginal)
12-month POP-Q stage 2 or higher in any compartment among examined women; risk difference in percentage points (laparoscopic minus vaginal)
results.note: Most anatomical failures were in the anterior compartment.

results.measure: Repeat surgery for apical prolapse by 12 months; intention to treat with last observation carried forward; risk difference in percentage points (laparoscopic minus vaginal)

harms.label: Persistent overactive bladder among women symptomatic before surgery
harms.note: At 12 months; bothersome overactive bladder UDI median 11 (IQR 0–22) versus 0 (0–11), exploratory P=0.012.

harms.label: Persistent fecal incontinence
harms.note: At 12 months; bothersome fecal-incontinence DDI scores differed, exploratory P=0.017.

harms.label: Dyspareunia among sexually active women
harms.note: At 12 months; exploratory P=0.042. De novo dyspareunia: 3 versus 5 women, respectively; difference not significant.

delivery.label: Laparoscopic technique
delivery.value: Bifurcated polypropylene Gynemesh passed through broad-ligament windows; permanent sutures to anterior and posterior cervix; titanium staples to sacral promontory; peritoneal closure.
delivery.note: Anterior and posterior vaginal repair could be performed laparoscopically or vaginally if indicated.

delivery.label: Vaginal technique
delivery.value: Posterior vaginal incision, pararectal dissection, permanent Prolene sutures through right sacrospinous ligament and posterior cervix.
delivery.note: Associated colporrhaphy or anti-incontinence surgery allowed.

delivery.label: Concomitant anterior wall repair
delivery.note: In the laparoscopic arm, 44 repairs were laparoscopic and 11 vaginal; all in the vaginal arm were anterior colporrhaphy.

delivery.label: Assigned laparoscopic surgery not received
delivery.value: 6/64: 5 received vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy and 1 a Manchester-Fothergill procedure.
delivery.note: Technical difficulties included adhesions, adiposity limiting promontory visualization, enlarged uterus, vaginal perforation, and hard promontory tissue.

delivery.label: Hysterectomy after incidental endometrial cancer
delivery.note: A polyp removed during laparoscopic surgery contained endometrial carcinoma; total laparoscopic hysterectomy followed two months later.
